newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei ends down but holds above 18,000.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei ends down but holds above 18,000.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key barometer closed lower on Thursday but kept its nose above the psychologically important 18,000 level. Brokers said the market had not recovered completely from a tumble in the banking sector on Wednesday, although global blue-chips were sought.
The Nikkei 225 average ended 147.54 points or 0.81 percent lower at 18,038.43. Its March futures were in backwardation, a fall of 150 points taking them below the cash price to 18,030.
"More sales related to the fiscal year-end are expected and the outlook is far from optimistic," said Shinichi Ichikawa, strategist at Credit Lyonnais Securities.
"But it seems more and more unlikely that the Nikkei average will plunge to the 14,000 level, as initially expected," Ichikawa said.

He said a sell-off of bank shares was continuing but the impact on the market was not as large as in the past. Investors were interested in global issues, which was also helping halt the Nikkei average's losses.

Blue-chip favourite Sony Corp, which announced strong consolidated business results for the third quarter of fiscal 1996/97 on Wednesday, succeeded in pushing the benchmark briefly into positive territory in the morning.
It ended the session up 140 yen at 8,360.

Brokers said, however, that due to lingering concerns about the financial health of banks, investors were opting for a low profile. Most of the day's trade was steered by arbitrage-related activity, they said.
Turnover expanded to 393 million issues from 381 million on Wednesday. Losers outnumbered winners 685 to 388, while 169 issues were unchanged.
The yen's retreat to near 124 yen to the dollar did not inspire buying of export-related shares as the market wants to see just how the firms' earnings will benefit, brokers said.
But Toyota Motor managed to edge higher, adding 30 yen to end at 3,100 yen.
Nippon Credit Bank Ltd gained 20 yen to 201 after the bank denied market rumours about its financial health late on Wednesday. The rumours had driven the shares to a lifetime low.

Yamaha Corp jumped after it said it would announce the signing of an original equipment manufacturing (OEM) contract with a U.S. chip maker. The shares ended at a new fiscal year high, rising 50 yen to 2,130.
Speculative shares lost ground, dampening sentiment as a whole, brokers said. Daido Steel Sheet Corp shed 173 yen to 847. Construction firm Arai-Gumi Ltd fell 200 yen to 1,060.
By sector, gainers were headed by gas, miscellaneous manufacturers, fisheries, communications and retailers.
Mining, construction, electric power, securities and iron/steel led the group of declining sectors.
The broader TOPIX index fell 5.52 points or 0.41 percent to 1,349.88. The Nikkei 300 was down 0.97 point or 0.38 percent to 257.09 at the end of the session.
The second sector index was down 6.7 points or 0.39 percent at 1,731,35 in a turnover of 7.86 million shares, compared with Wednesday's 11.9 million shares traded.
In late afternoon Tokyo, the over-the-counter market was down 9.08 points or 0.71 percent at 1,267.07.
--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-9052
